subject.title: feat(onboarding): recommend plugins and skills from installed apps

question: Should onboarding send installed-app metadata to the configured model and ClawHub by default after disclosure, or must users explicitly consent before that outbound matching begins?
rationale: The branch deliberately chooses a default-on privacy posture for new external metadata transfer; code review cannot decide that product and trust-policy boundary safely.

options.title: Require consent before matching
options.body: Prompt before sending app metadata, respect the existing discovery-access choice where appropriate, and strip paths and unnecessary identifiers from every outbound payload.

options.title: Approve disclosure-only matching
options.body: Explicitly accept default-on outbound matching, then accurately disclose every transmitted field and document the privacy and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Split and pause recommendations
options.body: Land the independent setup-inference fix separately while holding the installed-app recommendation and node inventory surfaces for a narrower design review.

recommendation.title: Require consent before matching
recommendation.body: Prompt before sending app metadata, respect the existing discovery-access choice where appropriate, and strip paths and unnecessary identifiers from every outbound payload.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision concerns the onboarding redesign and privacy behavior that this project and feature owner explicitly documented in the branch.
